properties.title: Neural operator-based digital twins for modeling amyloid-β and tau propagation and treatment optimization in Alzheimer's disease

membership.reason: Hybrid mechanistic reaction-diffusion PDE + LENO neural operator digital twin for cortical amyloid-beta and tau propagation coupled to PDE-constrained optimal control.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L4 decision/control-coupled hybrid organ world model (WT_ORGAN, BP_CONTROLLER).

properties.backbone: Laplace-Beltrami eigenspace projection (P modes) + reaction-diffusion PDE + shallow tanh neural reaction operator (LENO) + transfer-learning personalization

properties.flow: Longitudinal ADNI PET -> FreeSurfer cortical surface -> LENO reaction-diffusion digital twin -> forward-backward adjoint optimal control C*(t) -> VR visualization

properties.purpose: Spatiotemporal prediction of amyloid-beta/tau pathology and personalized optimal-control dosing design in Alzheimer's disease.
properties.environment: Retrospective ADNI longitudinal PET cohort (111 amyloid-beta, 25 tau subjects)

assertions.rationale: PET-MRI registration, cerebellar SUVR normalization, and FreeSurfer fsaverage cortical surface resampling.
Spectral projection onto truncated Laplace-Beltrami eigenbasis (P in {1500, 2048, 4096}).
Spectral state vector beta(t) representing cortical biomarker concentration u(x,t).
Transfer-learning fine-tuning of population LENO model onto individual subject longitudinal PET scans.
Continuous therapeutic control/dosing intensity C(t) entering reaction-diffusion dynamics.

In-silico comparison of optimal treatment C*(t) versus untreated (C=0) trajectories from the same initial patient states across 111 amyloid-beta and 25 tau digital twins (Fig. 5, pp. 4-6), under a prescribed analytical clearance term -C(t)u rather than observed clinical treatment data.
Continuous-time reaction-diffusion PDE evolution over cortical manifold.
Mechanistic Laplace-Beltrami diffusion + learned LENO nonlinear reaction operator.
Biomarker dynamics modulated by therapeutic control term -C(t)u.
Surface reaction-diffusion PDE d_t u - D Delta_Gamma u = F(u).
Combines known cortical diffusion operator with data-driven neural reaction operator.

Forward biomarker propagation is evaluated on reserved final PET scans for subjects with >=3 time points, achieving 87% accuracy for amyloid-beta and 81% for tau (Sec. 3.2 p. 8; Fig. 3 p. 4; Tables 2-3 p. 9).
PDE-constrained optimal control solved via forward-backward adjoint sweep over the learned LENO dynamics.

Forward-backward sweep PDE-constrained optimal control C*(t) = -p(t)^T beta(t) / (2 alpha(t)) is evaluated in silico at population level (Fig. 4) and across 111 amyloid-beta and 25 tau patient twins versus untreated progression (Fig. 5); treatment term -C(t)u and side-effect penalties alpha(t) are prescribed analytically, not clinically validated.
Patient-specific Alzheimer's progression prediction and personalized treatment optimization.
Relative L2 spectral/physical prediction accuracies: 87.7-88.2% amyloid-beta, 82.4-82.5% tau on ADNI test splits.
Patient-specific transfer learning and individualized treatment-reduction curves across 111 amyloid-beta and 25 tau subjects (Fig. 5).
Optimal-control dosing achieves ~50% mean biomarker reduction across subjects under prescribed cost functional (Fig. 5).

evidence_fragments.content: Using this framework, we achieve predictive accuracies of 87% for amyloid-β and 81% for tau. Building on the learned dynamics, we further formulate a PDE-constrained optimal control problem to design personalized therapeutic strategies that regulate pathological protein propagation.

Longitudinal neuroimaging measurements of amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau on the cortical surface are integrated with a reaction–diffusion model to construct a patient-specific digital twin. In the forward mode, the framework learns biomarker dynamics from sparse longitudinal observations and predicts the spatiotemporal progression of pathology. In the backward mode, the learned digital twin is coupled with PDE-constrained optimal control to identify personalized therapeutic interventions that regulate disease evolution.

Patient-specific treatment effects predicted by the learned digital twin for amyloid-β (top, 111 subjects) and tau (bottom, 25 subjects). Left: Final biomarker concentration with treatment versus without treatment for individual subjects in the left and right hemispheres. The dashed line indicates equality; points below the line represent treatment-induced reduction. Right: Distribution of percentage reductions across subjects, with horizontal bars indicating cohort means.
We then adopt a forward–backward sweep method to solve the optimal control problem. The full derivation of the above optimality system and the algorithm are provided in SI Appendix 6.

For model evaluation on prediction accuracy, we use patients with at least three time points. For these patients, all but the final time point are used for training, and the last available scan is reserved for evaluation of prediction accuracy.

For each patient, we compute two trajectories: one under the optimal treatment strategy and one without treatment (C ≡ 0). The resulting trajectories are compared in terms of final biomarker burden to quantify the predicted treatment effect, as shown in Fig. 5.

capability_assessments.rationale: Hybrid reaction-diffusion PDE + LENO neural operator digital twin implements persistent spectral cortical state, continuous-time dynamics, and learned nonlinear reaction kinetics, with held-out final-scan retrospective forecasting evaluated on ADNI PET (87% amyloid-beta, 81% tau) and PDE-constrained forward-backward optimal control evaluated in silico across 111 amyloid-beta and 25 tau patient twins (~50% mean simulated burden reduction vs untreated, Fig. 5), satisfying L4 in-silico optimal control. Importantly, treatment dynamics (-C(t)u) and side-effect penalties alpha(t) are prescribed analytically rather than learned from interventional clinical data, so in-silico L4 control does not establish clinical treatment efficacy.

limitations: Amyloid-beta and tau are modeled independently due to lack of paired longitudinal scans; treatment side-effect penalties are prescribed rather than data-inferred.
Optimal-control treatment reductions are in-silico model projections on retrospective ADNI twins, not prospective trial outcomes.

legacy_cells.B: Neural operator-based digital twins for modeling amyloid-β and tau propagation and treatment optimization in Alzheimer's disease
legacy_cells.C: Xu, Xiaofeng, Dan, Tingting, Zhou, Zifan, Li, Bin, Wu, Guorong, Hao, Wenrui
legacy_cells.O: Alzheimer’s disease; amyloid-β and tau pathology
legacy_cells.S: Can cortical amyloid-β and tau trajectories be predicted from longitudinal PET data, and can modeled treatment-intensity schedules reduce their predicted burden?
legacy_cells.T: ADNI participants with longitudinal amyloid-β or tau PET; after projection-error filtering, 111 amyloid-β subjects and 25 tau subjects; prediction testing required at least three time points.
legacy_cells.U: Computational researchers and clinicians (VR platform context)
legacy_cells.V: Choose a modeled treatment-intensity trajectory that trades off predicted biomarker burden against a prescribed treatment side-effect penalty.
legacy_cells.AI: Longitudinal amyloid-β PET; longitudinal tau PET; cortical-surface biomarker fields
legacy_cells.AS: P = 4096 Laplace–Beltrami spectral coefficients in the reported main configuration
legacy_cells.AZ: State is represented as cortical amyloid-β or tau concentration fields and visualized on cortical surfaces; spectral modes are also analyzed.
legacy_cells.BD: Continuous dosing intensity C(t), optimized over time and constrained to be nonnegative.
legacy_cells.BL: Semi-implicit time discretization with t_n = nΔt and Δt = T/N; physical units for T are not stated in the extracted text.
legacy_cells.BN: Reaction–diffusion dynamics on the cortical manifold, using a Laplace–Beltrami diffusion operator and a learned nonlinear reaction term.
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted amyloid-β and tau concentration fields/trajectories on cortical surfaces; optimized treatment-control trajectories and corresponding modeled biomarker responses.
legacy_cells.BU: PDE-constrained objective J = ∫[‖β(t)‖₂² + α(t)C(t)²]dt: minimize biomarker burden plus a treatment-intensity penalty representing prescribed side effects/cost.
legacy_cells.BV: Neural-operator training minimizes data loss plus discretized-PDE residual loss (L = L_D + L_R); control minimizes the PDE-constrained burden-plus-penalty objective.
legacy_cells.CK: Minimize integrated squared biomarker-state magnitude plus α(t)C(t)², subject to the learned reaction–diffusion dynamics; controls are constrained nonnegative.
legacy_cells.DQ: After filtering: 111 amyloid-β subjects and 25 tau subjects; pre-filter cohorts were 124 and 62 subjects, respectively.
legacy_cells.DX: Test Acc1 (spectral coefficient accuracy): amyloid-β 87.7 ± 3.9% left, 88.2 ± 3.6% right; tau 82.5 ± 2.3% left, 82.4 ± 1.6% right. Test Acc2 (physical-space accuracy): amyloid-β 87.2 ± 3.9% left, 87.7 ± 3.6% right; tau 81.1 ± 2.7% left, 81.0 ± 2.1% right (mean ± SD).
legacy_cells.EB: Optimal-control simulations compare treatment with untreated trajectories; the paper reports suppression of modeled amyloid-β and tau progression under treatment.
legacy_cells.EC: The adjoint forward–backward-sweep solver attained the lowest objective value and fastest convergence among the three tested numerical control solvers; no clinical decision-quality outcome was measured.
legacy_cells.FB: Explicit biomarker concentration fields on the cortical surface, represented in a truncated Laplace–Beltrami spectral basis; the model state is the coefficient vector β(t).
legacy_cells.FL: Longitudinal PET surface maps → projection into a truncated Laplace–Beltrami basis → LENO learns the nonlinear reaction term in reaction–diffusion dynamics → spectral-state biomarker trajectories; a PDE-constrained forward–backward-sweep optimizer computes treatment intensity C(t). VR renders the predicted fields and trajectories.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors combine cortical-surface reaction–diffusion modeling, LENO operator learning from longitudinal PET, PDE-constrained treatment optimization, and VR visualization in an Alzheimer’s disease digital-twin framework.
legacy_cells.FN: Reported test accuracy was 87.2%/87.7% for amyloid-β and 81.1%/81.0% for tau in physical space (left/right hemispheres; mean values in Table 1). Treatment-control simulations showed lower modeled biomarker burden than untreated trajectories.
legacy_cells.FO: Amyloid-β and tau were modeled independently in the main study because sufficiently paired longitudinal measurements were unavailable, so coupled reaction dynamics were not identifiable from the data. Treatment side-effect penalties were prescribed rather than inferred from patient-specific risk profiles or tolerance.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors identify data-driven estimation of treatment cost functionals as future work and note that the framework could extend to coupled, vector-valued dynamics when suitable paired multimodal longitudinal data are available.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors state that nonlinear aggregation/reaction mechanisms are incompletely understood and must be inferred from sparse, noisy, heterogeneous longitudinal neuroimaging observations.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper demonstrates retrospective PET-based prediction and mathematical in-silico control only. It does not establish identified clinical treatment effects, drug-specific dose semantics, prospective patient benefit, clinical deployment, or closed-loop treatment execution; treatment penalties are prescribed assumptions, not patient-derived risks.
